results.summary:
A client Services showcase already exists and ships today (`components/tahi/portal/services/portal-services.tsx`, 565 lines, plan panel + catalogue cards + Ask sheet). MR.7 (TASKS.md:161) asks for a brand-forward redesign of exactly that surface, and CL.3 (TASKS.md:167) adds tasteful upsell on top; CL.3 is blocked on CT.11 (TASKS.md:93, the catalogue is global with no orgId).

What a redesign can actually draw on, in four buckets:

1. CATALOGUE. `db/schema.ts:1811` `services` is thin: name, description, price (cents), currency, isRecurring, recurringInterval, showInCatalog, category ('service'|'topup'|'addon'). No orgId, no outcome/inclusions/timeline/imagery, no "who it is for". `lib/portal-service-view.ts` already synthesises those from the one free-text `description` field by convention (first paragraph = outcome, `- `/`* `/`• ` lines = inclusions, a `Timeline:` line = timeline) and derives a delivery badge (Ongoing / Add on / Top up / Project) so no price is ever shown. The portal route (`app/api/portal/services/route.ts:31-44`) deliberately projects away price and currency. Anything richer than that (hero image, "who it is for", from-price) needs a schema change, which is CT.11's natural home.

2. PLAN MODEL. Two competing sources. The REAL one is the settings-K/V plan catalogue: `lib/plan-catalog.ts:36` `loadPlanCatalog` merges `plan_catalog` JSON over `DEFAULT_PLAN_COPY` (`lib/plan-catalog-shared.ts:43`), giving `{id, name, tag, feats[], rec, monthlyRate, trackRate}` — admin-edited in Settings > Client plans. It ships only Maintain (NZ$1,500 base / $1,000 track) and Scale ($4,000 / $1,500). `lib/plan-utils.ts:172` `getPlanLabel` knows six plan ids (maintain, scale, tune, launch, hourly, custom) but only maintain and scale have prices, Stripe products (`lib/stripe-plans.ts:80`), track entitlements or catalogue copy. Tune/Launch/Hourly/Custom exist only as labels and dropdown options. Add-ons live in `lib/billing.ts:44` `CYCLE_BUNDLED_ADDONS` (monthly none, quarterly seo_dashboard, annual seo_dashboard + extra_track + priority_support) valued at `ADDON_VALUES` (150 / 500 / 350).

3. USAGE DATA PER CLIENT. Available: tracks and occupancy (`/api/portal/capacity`, `/api/portal/tracks`), requests delivered in the last 30 days with `deliveredAt` + `createdAt` (capacity route lines 81-101, which `lib/track-stats.ts:39` turns into count + average turnaround days), the full delivered history via `/api/portal/requests?status=delivered&limit=500`, recent files (`/api/portal/files`), upcoming calls (`/api/portal/calls`), and the activity pulse (`/api/portal/activity`). NOT available: time logged. `timeEntries` appears in 17 admin routes and zero portal routes. The richest usage model in the codebase (`/api/admin/reports/retainer-health`, which computes utilizationPct, requestsLast30d/90d, churnRiskScore and an explicit `upsellSignal`) is admin-only and would need a portal twin.

4. THE BRAND-FORWARD LOOK. Sign-in (`components/tahi/auth-shell.tsx`) and onboarding (`components/tahi/onboarding-shell.tsx`) share one scene: an always-dark forest panel with a canvas neon leaf, grain, bloom, wordmark, pill, headline, testimonial and a trust avatar row, next to a light card. Onboarding's plan step (`components/tahi/onboarding-content.tsx:516-546`) is the closest existing thing to what MR.7 wants: outcome line, big price, feature ticks, a "Recommended" pill, an add-on toggle with its own price, and a value anchor line ("Hiring the equivalent specialists separately runs $5,200 to $17,500+ a month"). Both scenes hardcode their colours by design (like the sidebar), unlike the current Services page which is all CSS-var tokens.

The upsell plumbing already exists and does not need inventing: `POST /api/portal/subscription/change-request` (plan or extra tracks, notifies every admin, writes audit, never mutates billing), the change-plan grid in `components/tahi/settings/sections/plan.tsx:341-350`, `getUpgradeGhostTracks` (`lib/plan-utils.ts:216`) which already writes the Maintain→Scale and priority-support upsell copy, and `PortalAskSheet` (`components/tahi/portal/portal-money-kit.tsx:315`) which files a real request or falls back to mailto. What is missing for CL.3 is the brief (Liam owes it), per-org scoping, and any notion of "who this service is for".

/tracks is built but unreachable for clients. app/(dashboard)/tracks/page.tsx + tracks-content.tsx render the per-track mini-kanban with ghost upsell cards, but Tracks is not in CLIENT_NAV (components/tahi/nav-model.tsx:125-152). The `services` table cannot answer CL.3's brief as it stands: 'who it is for' and 'from price' have no column, and the price it does have is a single flat cents value with no 'from' semantics. lib/portal-service-view.ts's description-parsing convention is an explicit stopgap (its header says 'none of that can land tonight (no schema change, no migration)'), not a design to build on.

No portal endpoint exposes hours, utilisation or any per-month usage rollup. 'How they are using it' has to be assembled client-side from /api/portal/capacity (30-day window) and /api/portal/requests?status=delivered, or a new portal report route has to be written. The admin retainer-health endpoint cannot be reused directly: it is isTahiAdmin-gated and iterates every org.

Do not model the showcase's plan copy on components/tahi/onboarding-content.tsx:67 PLANS. That array is hardcoded and does not read the plan_catalog settings key, so it silently diverges from what Settings > Client plans publishes. The server-side source of truth is lib/plan-catalog.ts loadPlanCatalog, surfaced to the client via /api/portal/subscription's `plans` field.

Tune, Launch, Hourly and Custom cannot be shown as purchasable plans. They exist as labels in lib/plan-utils.ts:172 and lib/utils.ts:20 and as admin dropdown options, but they have no catalogue entry, no monthly rate, no track entitlement (getTrackEntitlements returns all zeros) and no Stripe price. A client on one of those plan types renders 'No plan'-shaped capacity today.

Its content included 'client money pinned to the client's currency with no switcher'. So the Services plan panel still formats the monthly rate through useDisplayCurrency (portal-services.tsx:357), and any redesign should not assume the currency-pinning behaviour landed.

results.summary:
The studio invoices surface is two big client components (invoice-list.tsx 1381 lines, invoice-detail.tsx 1348 lines) sitting behind server pages that fork admin vs portal at the top (`app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx:27`, `[id]/page.tsx:25`) — a Tahi login with the `tahi-impersonate-org` cookie is routed to the portal components, so the studio branch never has to render a client view (the `!isAdmin` code paths inside both files are now dead weight for the admin surface but still shape the columns and mobile cards).

LIST: PageHeader with three actions (Export CSV, Import from Stripe, Create invoice), a FilterBar (search + Status multiselect + Source multiselect) plus a hand-rolled inline "Due:" date-range pair, and a `DataTable` with six admin columns (Client, Amount, Status, Source, Due, Created). No row actions, no selection, no bulk bar, no pagination — it fetches `?status=all` (server caps at 50) and filters entirely client-side. The New Invoice slide-over is the sophisticated part: IC.3 landed a resolver (`lib/invoice-defaults.ts`) that lands destination/currency/due-date from the picked client once per pick, with a three-state "known / pending / unknown" rail model and two different warning sentences depending on whether the client names a rail or inherits the studio default.

DETAIL: breadcrumb, a big-amount header card with a status pill, an eight-slot metadata grid, admin pay-page links (Stripe + Xero side by side), a flat row of up to eight admin actions, a persistent push-back outcome line, an AI Chase email card (generate / edit / send / regenerate / dismiss), read-only Notes, and a hand-rolled line-items table with subtotal / GST / discount / total. Feedback is split across three idioms: toast (`showToast`), inline `role="status"` sentences (send result, push-back), and eight native `alert()` / two `confirm()` calls.

BACK END: six routes under `app/api/admin/invoices/**` plus the CSV export and the hourly Xero export. IC.1–IC.5 are shipped and the money semantics are unusually carefully reasoned (paidAt/sentAt normalisation, forward-only Xero mapping, mark-paid push-back to the rail with reported skip reasons, Xero-rail email mode). What is still open is exactly what TASKS.md says: CT.14/IC.7 invoice numbers (no `invoices.number` column, `invoice_number_prefix` has zero readers, three different renderings of "the invoice number" in the codebase) and CT.13/IC.6 the hourly Xero export guard (no idempotency, no billing-model filter, hardcoded NZD, silent zero-rate skip).

For a redesign the highest-value structural findings are: (1) Delete Invoice is offered on ANY status including paid, and the route has no draft-only guard despite its own comment, so one click can erase revenue /financial-reports keys off `paid_at`; (2) a `viewed` invoice has no Mark as Paid button and a `paid` or `written_off` invoice has no un-do; (3) nothing on the page can edit amounts, line items, due date or notes after creation; (4) Export CSV ignores every active filter and, unlike the list GET, applies no team-member org scoping; (5) `xero-sync` applies no org scoping at all; (6) the invoices row already carries `reconciliationStatus` / `airwallexTxnId` that no invoice surface reads.

Portal counterparts live at components/tahi/portal/invoices/portal-invoice-list.tsx (744 lines) and portal-invoice-detail.tsx (743 lines).

DEAD BRANCH: both studio components still carry full `!isAdmin` code paths (invoice-list.tsx:882 `isAdmin = isAdminProp && !isImpersonatingClient`, the Pay column at :1133-1152, InvoiceMobileCard at :149-212, the portal-denial branch at :1173-1186; invoice-detail.tsx:191, the client pay CTA at :423-461, the denial branch at :274-290). AMOUNT CONVERSION IS FRAGILE: invoice-list.tsx:1072 renders the secondary currency line as `formatNativeWithDisplay(...).split('≈ ')[1] ?? ''` — string-splitting a formatted string on a literal approximately-equals. invoice-detail.tsx:381 does the same.

Softer notes worth a look: the page carries three different subtitles across states; the two usage charts answer different windows (90 days, 22 vs Apr to Sep, 33) under one headline; "Fits Scale" promotes a card into the feature slot without the why that justifies the slot; the 1280 feature art is 320x460 of wash holding a 320x240 motif; and at 375 the page is 7397px with twelve ask affordances, which is closer to a shop than the copy claims. Method: rendered the designer's archive/scratch/portal-services-scratch.html and walked 1280 and 375, light and dark, through ready, loading, member_seat, empty, error, feature_off, read-only, both catalogue scopes and the ask sheet. No project files were changed. Console is clean.

issues: BLOCKING: the row action menu on the bottom rows is clipped out of existence. .inv-card sets overflow:hidden and .inv-menu is an absolutely positioned child with no flip-up logic. Measured on the last row of the Owed view at 1280: menu height 242px, extending 231px past the card's bottom edge and 192px past .inv-scroll. The dots button visibly toggles to its open state and nothing appears. Void / Mark as paid / Resend / Copy link are unreachable on roughly the last three rows of every view, and the row menu is the only path to those actions on mobile. Fix: render the menu in a portal, or add an 'up' variant plus a flip check, or drop overflow:hidden from .inv-card and clip the corners another way.

The rail chip truncates the very state it exists to show. .inv-rail-s has text-overflow:ellipsis and the Rail column is a fixed 8.5rem, so at 1280 Mahana Orchards reads 'Manual • bank tran...' in both light and dark. Decision 1 says the chip carries the pay-link state as the one-glance answer; the longest state string is the one that gets eaten. The full text only exists in a title tooltip, which is a hover-only affordance and absent on touch. Widen the column, shorten the state vocabulary, or wrap.

375: every icon-only button measures 32 x 32px (.inv-iconbtn), including the header More menu and every row's action menu. Export and New invoice measure 36px tall. CLAUDE.md requires 44px minimum and this file's own header comment claims 2.75rem targets. The row dots at 32px is the sole entry to per-invoice actions on a phone.

375: the four totals tiles drop to one per row (@container inv max-width:48rem), so roughly 430px of money tiles plus the header sit above the saved-view rail and the first invoice never appears on a first screen. The 2-up grid used between 48rem and 64rem would hold at 375 and keep the strip to two rows.

375: the saved-view rail becomes a horizontal scroller with scrollbar-width:thin, which paints a desktop scrollbar track with arrow buttons inside the card (clearly visible in both light and dark). Other modules hide it. Also .inv-view-t small is hidden in that mode, so the money figure disappears from the saved views on the exact width where the tiles already ate the space.
375: .inv-search is 44px tall but the input inside it is only 18px and has no label or click handler on the wrapper, so the top and bottom 13px of the search field are dead to touch.
Nit: the header's More menu is a bare dots glyph with no border sitting between an outlined Export and a filled New invoice. It reads as an unfinished third button rather than an overflow affordance.

The metadata grid renders ghost cells. .inv-metas uses grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(10rem,1fr)) with gap:1px over a --border-subtle background, so any unfilled cell in the last row shows as a solid slab of border colour. TS-1045 at 1280 leaves five empty cells; TS-1041 in dark leaves six and reads as a broken block; at 375 (2 columns, 9 items) it leaves one. Fix: give .inv-meta:last-child a grid-column:1/-1 fill, or draw the hairlines with inset shadows the way the rest of this file does.

The hero's 'ONE next action' is immediately duplicated. On TS-1045 the hero button reads 'Approve it in Xero' with the sentence 'It is sitting at DRAFT in Xero, so Xero has not issued a pay page. Approve it in Xero.' and the Note directly beneath repeats that sentence verbatim under the title 'The client has no way to pay this' with a second button labelled 'Open Xero'. Two buttons, two labels, one job, stacked. Either drop the Note when the hero action already covers it, or strip the hero sentence to the reason and let the Note carry the fix.

The Bank transfer pay card leads with 'No page yet' for a manual invoice, which is the one case where the client CAN pay. The account number is demoted to the caption under a headline that says the opposite. Give the manual rail its own headline (the account number, or 'Bank transfer, no hosted page').

On a manual invoice, 'What the client sees' shows three cards of which two are permanent 'This invoice does not run on Stripe / Xero' filler. Consider showing only the rails in play plus the one that is missing.

Keyboard: the collapsed Danger zone stays in the tab order. .inv-danger-b.closed is grid-template-rows:0fr with overflow:hidden on the child, so the Void and Delete buttons keep tabIndex 0 and are focusable while the panel measures 0px high. Verified: focusing Void succeeded and scrolled the container. A keyboard user tabbing the Actions section lands on an invisible Void button and Enter opens the confirm. Add inert or visibility:hidden, or unmount when closed.

Hover: a disabled danger button dissolves. .inv-btn:disabled:hover (0,3,0) beats .inv-btn.danger (0,2,0) and there is no .inv-btn.danger:disabled:hover override (only .primary and .outline have one). Verified by cloning the rule as a class: rest state rgb(167,58,49) on white text, hovered state rgba(0,0,0,0) on rgb(18,26,15). The disabled Delete goes from solid red to transparent under the cursor. .ghost has the same gap.
Nit: the 'why it is disabled' sentence in .inv-act small is --text-faint inside a container at opacity .55, which is the lowest-contrast text on the page and it is the text carrying the explanation.

BLOCKING: clicking the client card clears the client. Field renders a <label> around composite controls with no htmlFor, so the label's implicit control becomes the first labelable descendant. In the picked state that is the 'Change client' close button. Verified live: picked Kowtow, clicked the client name, the selection was wiped. Clicking a chosen client to check it is the most natural gesture in that row.

BLOCKING: clicking the 'Where it goes' caption silently resets the payment rail. Same label cause, first labelable descendant is the first Seg radio. Verified live: destination set to 'Stripe link', clicked the caption, destination flipped to 'Dashboard only'. This is a money-routing field being reset by a click on a caption. Same mechanism makes 'Currency' and 'Payment terms' captions open their dropdowns. Fix Field once: render a div plus a span caption unless htmlFor is supplied.

The slide over's primary CTA is disabled with no reason anywhere. Verified: the Create invoice button has disabled=true and title=null, and there is no inline note. Decision 7 says every disabled control states its reason in place; the one control the whole panel exists to reach is the exception. The footer note says 'Created as a draft. Sending is a separate step.', which answers a different question. Say 'Pick a client and add at least one line'.

Note on the pattern generally: reasons delivered only via title on a disabled button do not render in Chrome (disabled controls do not fire mouse events) and never render on touch. The list and detail both carry a footnote fallback for the read-only case, but the row-menu and Btn title reasons do not.

SlideOver and Confirm handle Escape, move focus to the panel and stop the overlay mousedown correctly, but neither traps focus or restores focus to the trigger on close, and background scroll is not locked.

The draft signs the wrong person. TS-1043 is owned by Staci Bonnie (shown in the metadata grid on the same page) and the generated body ends 'Thanks,\nLiam'. Verified across samples: the sign-off is hardcoded and ignores inv.owner. On a client-facing email in a two-person studio this is the kind of error that gets noticed.

The firmer variant auto-writes a commercial commitment: 'If I do not hear back this week I will pause new work on the account until it is settled.' That is a policy decision being pre-drafted as if it were settled. Worth a switch, or softer default wording, since the drafter is one click from Send.

Otherwise strong: the idle copy states how many times the invoice has been chased and that the tone escalates, the drafting state uses a skeleton plus an honest 'Reading the invoice, the account and the last three notes', the model and token count are shown, and nothing sends without an explicit press. The teal AI accent reads as intentional rather than decorative.

The loading state asserts facts it does not have. While the table shows skeleton rows, the totals strip renders real tiles reading NZ$0 with the sub-lines 'Nothing out', 'Nothing past due', 'Nothing settled yet in September', 'No drafts waiting', and every saved view shows a 0 count and NZ$0. On a money surface that is a false statement during the first second, not a placeholder. Skeleton the tiles and the view counts too, or blank the sub-lines until state === 'ready'.

Framing is inconsistent across the three failure states. Empty renders inside .inv-card with a border; error and no-scope render bare on the page background with no container, and both also drop the totals strip and the saved-view rail entirely. Pick one frame.
Export and New invoice stay fully enabled in the error and no-scope states. Exporting from a ledger that did not load, or raising an invoice when no client is in scope, are both dead ends.

Good: the filtered-to-nothing state is well judged, distinguishing 'Nothing matches that' (with 'Clear the search') from 'Nothing in overdue' with the line 'That is good news, not an empty page'. The read-only teammate seat greys New invoice and carries the footnote 'You are reading the ledger. Only an owner can send an invoice or move money.' Private mode blurs the money and leaves the counts, which is the right cut.

Conformance is strong overall. Zero em or en dashes across all four files. Row hairlines are drawn as inset box-shadows rather than single-side borders (the same habit as ops.css). Leaf radius appears only on primary CTAs, avatar wrappers and small icon backgrounds. Manrope throughout, rem spacing throughout, --ease resolves, dark mode falls out of a paired token block and holds up at 1280 and 375. Domain colour is used with intent (money green, work slate, growth gold, teal for the AI section, danger red). prefers-reduced-motion is respected on the skeleton shimmer. No horizontal overflow at 375 (scrollWidth === clientWidth === 375). The .inv- prefix is genuinely unclaimed.

One single-side border remains: .inv-slide { border-left:1px solid var(--border) }. ops.css, the closest sibling module, has zero side borders, and this file avoids them everywhere else deliberately. Swap it for box-shadow:inset 1px 0 0 var(--border) for consistency with the file's own stated habit.

The .inv-btn.primary brand-tinted drop shadow matches ops.css, so it is in-house rather than a deviation. Noting it only because 'borders not shadows' is a stated rule and this is the one sanctioned exception.

The seventh saved view 'No way to pay' (owed plus missing or held pay link) earns its place. It is the only place the surface answers 'why has this client not paid' without opening anything, and it reads cleanly in both themes. Keep it.

The status vocabulary unification (Sent and Opened as one gold family, Draft slate, Overdue red, Paid green) and the D.pair() native-plus-display amount are both clear wins over a single formatted string, and the multi-currency rows (US$4,800 over NZ$7,968, A$1,890 over NZ$2,060) read correctly at every width.

results.summary:
Verdict: FIX, not REDO. This is the best-argued surface in the prototype so far and the vocabulary is right: soft cards, borders not shadows, leaf radius only where it belongs, Manrope, intentional domain colour, dark mode straight out of the tokens, no em dashes, no horizontal overflow at 375. The totals strip, the seven saved views, the rail chip carrying the pay-link state, the derived-once overdue, the D.pair() native/display amounts and the Confirm dialogs that name what survives all land. But it is not shippable as-is: I found two blocking interaction bugs plus a set of real defects, all verified live in the designer's scratch mount at 1280 and 375, light and dark, across every state.

Blocking, in order:
1. LIST. The row action menu is clipped out of existence on the bottom rows. .inv-card has overflow:hidden and .inv-menu is an absolutely positioned child with no flip logic. Measured on the last row: 242px menu, 231px past the card. The dots button toggles open and nothing renders. Void, Mark as paid and Resend are unreachable there, and on mobile that menu is the only route to them.
2. SLIDE OVER. Kit's Field wraps composite controls in a bare <label>, so the caption's implicit control is the first labelable descendant. Verified live: clicking the picked client's name wipes the client, and clicking the words "Where it goes" resets the payment rail from Stripe link back to Dashboard only. A money-routing field reset by a click on a caption.

Then: the detail's metadata grid renders ghost cells (auto-fit grid over a 1px border background) which read as a broken slab at 1280, 375 and worst in dark; the hero's "one next action" is immediately duplicated by a Note repeating the same sentence with a differently-labelled second button; the chase drafter signs "Thanks, Liam" on an invoice owned by Staci Bonnie and auto-writes "I will pause new work on the account until it is settled"; the collapsed Danger zone keeps Void and Delete in the tab order at 0px height; a disabled danger button turns transparent on hover because .inv-btn:disabled:hover has no .danger override; the loading state asserts NZ$0 and "Nothing out" while the table is still a skeleton; the rail chip ellipsises the pay state it exists to show ("Manual • bank tran..."); and at 375 every icon-only button is 32px against the 44px house minimum, with four full-width money tiles pushing the first invoice off the first screen.

Roughly a day of fixes, most of them one-line and several shared with the other modules (the Field label pattern and the disabled-danger hover gap almost certainly repeat in ops-kit.jsx and clients-kit.jsx, alongside the .outline utility collision the designer already found). Nothing here questions the design thinking; it is all the last mile.
